accountStepHint: Your FDAI identity and Microsoft 365 workflow identity can belong to different tenants. Keep the workflow owner account ready for Microsoft account selection.
accountUsageHint: This value is for copying only. It does not control Microsoft sign-in or infer the tenant, and FDAI does not store it.
accountInvalid: Enter a complete email-style user principal name.
workflowStep: Create or open the workflow in Power Automate
workflowStepHint: Power Automate uses the current Microsoft browser session. If it is not the account above, switch or sign out there, or open the link in a private browser window.
saveBoundary: A deployment stores the URL in a dedicated Key Vault secret. The local profile stores only encrypted ciphertext in its private Operator database. FDAI verifies the saved version before testing, never returns the URL, and never prefills it. Saving and testing do not activate runtime delivery.
saveTestStepHint: Paste the generated HTTP URL from Power Automate. FDAI saves and independently verifies a new binding version, then sends the bounded test card. Contributor, Approver, and Owner roles can see that a binding exists; nobody can read it back. Only an Owner can replace it.
bindingHidden: The saved URL is hidden for this role.
bindingMissing: No saved Teams Workflows URL is available. An Owner can save one.
contributorReadOnly: Visible to Contributor, Approver, and Owner roles as metadata only. Only an Owner can replace and test the value.
bindingNeverReturned: FDAI never returns the saved URL. Leave this field empty to keep the current binding, or paste a new URL to replace it.
bindingSavedDetail: Version {version} was saved and verified at {time}. Saving is not activation; a deployment still decides when A2 delivery uses this binding.
bindingSavedVersionOnly: Version {version} is saved. FDAI has no local save record for this version, and saving is not activation.
savedAndAcceptedDetail: The saved binding version was verified, then Power Automate accepted the test with HTTP {status} at {time}.
guideSummary: Show the Power Automate setup guide
guideIntro: Complete the following steps in Power Automate before pasting the callback URL into FDAI.
guideVerifyAccountBody: Open the account manager in the upper-right corner and confirm that the signed-in account matches:
guideCreateBody: In the left navigation, select Create. Under Start from blank, select Automated cloud flow.
guideCreateImageAlt: Power Automate with Create and the Automated cloud flow tile highlighted
guideCreateImageCaption: Select Create, then Automated cloud flow.
guideNameFlowTitle: Name the flow and skip trigger selection
guideNameFlowBody: Enter a recognizable Flow name, such as FDAI Teams Flow. Do not select a trigger in this dialog. Select Skip to open the flow designer.
guideNameFlowImageAlt: Build an automated cloud flow dialog with FDAI Teams Flow entered and Skip highlighted
guideNameFlowImageCaption: Enter the Flow name, then select Skip.
guideAddTriggerBody: In the flow designer, select Add a trigger.
guideAddTriggerImageAlt: Power Automate flow designer with Add a trigger highlighted
guideSelectTriggerTitle: Select the Microsoft Teams Webhook trigger
guideSelectTriggerBody: Select Microsoft Teams Webhook, then select When a Teams webhook request is received.
guideSelectTriggerImageAlt: Microsoft Teams Webhook trigger list showing When a Teams webhook request is received
guideSelectTriggerImageCaption: Select When a Teams webhook request is received.
guideConfigureTriggerBody: On Parameters, set Who can trigger the flow? to Anyone. The HTTP URL is generated only after the flow is saved. Anyone who has that URL can trigger the flow, so keep it secret and apply your tenant's workflow policy.
guideConfigureTriggerImageAlt: Teams webhook trigger parameters with Who can trigger the flow set to Anyone and an HTTP URL generated after save
guideConfigureTriggerImageCaption: Set Who can trigger the flow? to Anyone. The HTTP URL appears after save.
guideAddActionBody: Under the webhook trigger, select + to add an action. Select Microsoft Teams, then select Post card in a chat or channel.
guideAddActionImageAlt: Plus button highlighted below the Teams webhook trigger
guideAddActionImageCaption: Select + below the trigger to add a new action.
guideConfigureActionTitle: Configure the Teams destination and card
guideConfigureActionBody: Set Post as to Flow bot and Post in to Channel. Select the target Team and Channel. In Adaptive Card, insert the triggerBody() expression. The Team and Channel shown below are illustrative; select the actual notification destination.
guideConfigureActionImageAlt: Post card in a chat or channel action configured for Flow bot, Channel, a target Team and Channel, and the triggerBody expression
guideConfigureActionImageCaption: Select the target Team and Channel, then set Adaptive Card to triggerBody().
guideFinishTitle: Confirm the Flow name and save
guideFinishBody: Select the flow title at the top and confirm that the Flow name is the intended name. Update it if needed, then select Save in the upper-right corner.
guideFinishImageAlt: Power Automate command bar with the Save button highlighted
guideFinishImageCaption: Select Save in the upper-right corner.
guideCopyUrlBody: After the save succeeds, select When a Teams webhook request is received. Under Parameters, copy the generated HTTP URL and return to FDAI.
guideCopyUrlImageAlt: Saved Power Automate flow showing its title, the Teams webhook trigger, and the copy control beside a redacted HTTP URL
guideCopyUrlImageCaption: Confirm the Flow name, open the trigger, and copy the generated HTTP URL. The URL is redacted in this guide.
guideSecretNote: Treat the callback URL as a secret. Do not place it in source control, documentation, chat, or screenshots.
